title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000022: repository-root TRACEABILITY_DOCUMENT.md states ISO 26262 and IEC 61508 compliance evidence and an ASIL-D/ASIL-B capability, and lies outside the corpus write boundary

standards_mappings.rationale: The claim of compliance evidence is recorded here as an unverified reference. No corpus artifact supports it, and the corpus does not claim conformity anywhere.

lifecycle_status_note: 'reviewed': the remediation described below was performed and the resulting file was read back and checked. 'reviewed' here means the edit was verified to remove the claimed defects. It does NOT mean a human approved this finding or the document: human_approval_status remains 'pending' for every artifact.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Remediation performed. The repository owner explicitly authorized amending the repository-root file, widening the write boundary for this one file only. The conformity sentence, the IEC 61508 compliance claim and the ASIL capability statement were removed or restated; a non-conformity header was added; the ASIL values in the data tables were relabelled hypothetical; the standards table was retitled as a reference index; and the stale coverage table was marked stale. The authorization, the exact edits and the residual risk are recorded in remediation_performed and residual_risk.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Second remediation pass, after an independent adversarial review found the revision-2 fix incomplete. Verified defects and corrected: (1) a fabricated human-approval sign-off block (Reviewer/Approver/Status: APPROVED naming fictional corpus roles) survived at the end of the file and contradicted the READ FIRST header in the same file and all 220 corpus records - removed and replaced with a document-control table stating the real position; (2) the false provenance claim 'This document is automatically generated ... Manual edits will be overwritten on next generation' survived, which is false and told the next editor the authorised edits would be erased - replaced with a section stating the file is hand-authored, not generated, not under tool control, and therefore drift-prone; (3) two IEC 61508-3 clause rows survived in section 9 despite the revision-2 remediation record and commit message claiming they were removed, while the same revision's new section-9 preamble asserted the clause ids were the corpus's own references - rows removed and the preamble corrected; (4) the artifact-type definition table still carried a bare unqualified 'ASIL' at the point of definition - qualified; (5) several unmeasured '100%' and 'complete chain' coverage claims with no stated method were replaced by measured figures with named methods; (6) the STALE note pointed at the stale hand-written coverage-report.md as 'authoritative, tool-computed' - repointed at the live tool; (7) the mutation count contradicted the tool (said 6/20 functional, corpus.py check reports PASS for all 20) - corrected; (8) review and finding counts understated the corpus - scoped to their records and corpus-wide figures added; (9) the stated id scheme was wrong and several ids did not resolve - corrected; (10) scenario ids used the short key form inconsistently with the stated scheme - normalised. Also corrected beyond the review's list: a non-existent hazard id, four non-existent SW-TSR ids, a non-existent design id, a non-existent variant id, three non-existent baselines, a swapped parameter mapping, a mispaired test-measure-to-requirement mapping, a fabricated execution outcome, two duplicated glossary rows, a misnumbered section heading, and a '100% line/branch achieved' column with no coverage measurement behind it. This revision also corrects three stale fields in this record itself: the disposition_note asserted a corpus convention the corpus contradicts, the resolution still opened 'NOT RESOLVED, AND NOT RESOLVABLE', and root_cause/impact/resolution all still asserted that no functional or technical safety concept record exists.

subject_file_location: repository root, one level above docs/artifacts/
evidence: RETAINED REVISION-1 HISTORY - this field records what was observed when the finding was raised and must not be read as the current state of the file. The claims it makes about the file's contents described the file before remediation. See revision 3 of revision_history, remediation_performed, updated_evidence and resolution for the current state. Direct read of the file on 2026-09-29, lines as numbered in the file at that time. Line 19, under '1.1 Purpose', stated verbatim: 'Provides evidence for compliance with ISO 26262, IEC 61508, and other applicable safety standards'. Line 23, under '1.2 Scope', stated verbatim: 'Safety Requirements (ASIL-D, ASIL-B)'. Line 7 attributed the document to baseline commit 308028fb and line 8 stated 'Document Version: 1.0' dated 2026-09-11. One further defect found in the second review pass was not in revision 1: a document-control block near the end of the file recorded a named reviewer, a named approver and an approved status, an approval that had never taken place. Three independent checks contradicted or failed to support the claim. First, conformity: every indexed record carries human_approval_status 'pending', production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, and the acceptance suite's own gate 'no production_authorized/approved artifacts' passes precisely because nothing is approved. No certification, no tool qualification and no third-party assessment record exists in the corpus. Second, IEC 61508: a recursive search for the string '61508' across the whole of docs/artifacts returned no match in any record. The only two standards in governance/standards-lock.json are ISO_26262_2018 (edition 2018) and ASPICE_PAM_41 (edition 4.1), locked_by 'safety'. There is no IEC 61508 requirement, mapping, analysis or normative reference anywhere in the corpus, so the document claimed compliance evidence for a standard the corpus has never ingested or referenced. Third, ASIL: the corpus does carry ASIL field values, FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 with asil 'ASIL_D' and FB2-SAF-FSR-000004 with safety_allocation.asil 'ASIL_B', so the letters are not invented. But the asil field on FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 carries NO justification field, and the corpus's own validator raises an open finding for it - 'safety goal FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 ASIL ASIL_D lacks justification' - so the value is an unjustified field on a synthetic record, not a derivation. Revision 1 further recorded that the concept-phase records that would justify an ASIL D determination were absent. THAT PART OF REVISION 1 IS NOW OUTDATED: FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 exist as of 2026-09-29. Their existence is recorded in closure_note and does not change the remediation, because both concepts are synthetic and each states in its own limitations field that it establishes no ASIL capability for any real product. The ASIL field remains unjustified and is still flagged by the validator.
impact: RETAINED REVISION-1 HISTORY, with one premise corrected - see the sentence on the safety concepts below. Three distinct harms, in increasing order of seriousness. First, an internal contradiction: the document claimed compliance evidence while the corpus it describes is uniformly unapproved and unauthorized, so a reader who trusts the document will draw the opposite conclusion from the one the guard fields support. Second, a claim against a standard the corpus never engaged: naming IEC 61508 implies the lifecycle work was performed against a standard that was never locked, never mapped and never analysed in this corpus, which would misdirect any subsequent assessment activity toward work that has not been done. Note carefully what is and is not being alleged. foxBMS's own pinned documentation does list IEC 61508 as a candidate standard and cites IEC 61508-3:2010, so the standard is a legitimate consideration for the product and its removal from the sentence is not the remedy. The remedy is that the corpus performed no IEC 61508 work, so it cannot supply compliance evidence for it; if IEC 61508 engagement is wanted, the standard must first be added to the lock and the referenced records produced. This is what the revision-3 correction did: it removed the two IEC 61508-3 clause rows and added an explicit not-engaged note, rather than deleting the standard from the project's consideration. Third, and most serious for a safety corpus, an ASIL capability statement. Presenting 'ASIL-D' as an established characteristic of the corpus's safety requirements, when the asil field has no justification and the corpus's own validator flags it, is a safety-capability claim of exactly the kind this corpus exists to avoid making. A fourth harm was found in the second review pass and was worse than the first three in one specific way: a fabricated human-approval sign-off block near the end of the file named a reviewer and an approver and recorded the status as approved. An assessor who skimmed to that block got the exact opposite of the true state, and the fabrication was more likely to be believed than the disclaimer at the top of the file, because a sign-off block is what readers are trained to look for. The file also sits at the repository root rather than under docs/artifacts, so it is the most prominent document in the tree and the one most likely to be read first by a person who has not seen the generated views that carry the guard fields and the non-conformity disclaimer. No artifact was relabelled and no acceptance check was altered to accommodate this finding. CORRECTION TO REVISION 1: revision 1 recorded that the concept-phase records were absent. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 now exist, so that premise is no longer current; see closure_note. Their existence does not reduce the harm, because they are synthetic and disclaim any ASIL capability.
root_cause: RETAINED REVISION-1 HISTORY - the causal account still holds, with one premise corrected at the end. The document was authored at the repository root on 2026-09-11, during the period before the corpus had a generated view layer, and it was written as a summary of the corpus's ID scheme and link structure rather than as a governance-controlled document. It therefore never passed through the corpus's guard-field discipline: it carries no 'Derived, not authored' provenance header, no human_approval_status, no production_authorized field, and no statement of what the corpus does not claim, all of which the generated views carry. Three habits produced the specific overclaims. The first is conflating a standards MAPPING with a standards CONFORMITY claim: the corpus deliberately holds a mapping from artifacts to ISO 26262 clause references, and somewhere in drafting, 'maps to ISO 26262 Part 2' was written up as 'provides evidence for compliance with ISO 26262'. Structural mapping is not conformity, and the corpus states this explicitly in the standards-mapping view. The second is conflating a field VALUE with a DETERMINATION: FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 carries asil 'ASIL_D' with no justification field, and the document read that as evidence of an established ASIL D capability. The value is real and traceable to that record; what is missing is the derivation, and the corpus's own validator says so on every run. The third, found in the second review pass, is worse than the other two because it is not an overclaim at all: a document-control block was written with a named reviewer, a named approver and an approved status, and no such review or approval ever took place. The names were drawn from the corpus's own fictional role vocabulary (safety_engineer, safety_manager), so the fabrication looked internally consistent to anyone who had read a corpus record. The IEC 61508 reference has no traceable origin in any corpus record. It was most plausibly carried over from the pinned source's own safety documentation, which does list IEC 61508 as an example standard that might suit foxBMS users, and then converted from a candidate-standard mention into an asserted compliance claim during drafting. That conversion from 'a standard we might apply' to 'evidence for compliance' is the same category of error as the ISO 26262 claim, and it is the specific step that is unsupportable. Finally, the file's location is the proximate cause of all of this surviving. Because it was written outside docs/artifacts, it fell outside every control this corpus applies: the validator does not read it, the renderer does not regenerate it, and the guard-field and non-conformity rules that govern every generated surface have no reach over it. That last fact is also why the revision-2 fix was incomplete: nothing in the toolchain could detect that the pass had missed the sign-off block, the provenance claim and the IEC rows. CORRECTION TO REVISION 1: revision 1 attributed the missing derivation to the absence of concept-phase records. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 now exist, so the concept phase is no longer empty; the derivation is still missing, and the asil field is still unjustified, so the causal account stands with that premise replaced.
resolution: RESOLVED as of 2026-09-29, revision 3. The three defects an independent adversarial review confirmed were missed by the revision-2 fix, plus a set of further defects found by the same pass, are corrected and the file no longer contains them: the fabricated human-approval sign-off block is gone; the false 'automatically generated, manual edits will be overwritten' provenance claim is gone, replaced by a section stating the file is hand-authored, not generated, not read or rewritten by any tool, and therefore drift-prone; and the two IEC 61508-3 clause rows are gone, replaced by an explicit not-engaged note that keeps IEC 61508 in the project's consideration while stating that the corpus supplies nothing for it, together with a corrected section-9 preamble that no longer implies the removed rows were corpus references. The exact edits are in remediation_performed; the residuals are in residual_risk. WHAT IS NOT RESOLVED AND DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED HERE: (a) the file is still outside docs/artifacts, still hand-authored and still outside the toolchain's reach, so nothing in CI will detect a regression - that is residual_risk, it is not closed by this disposition, and closing it needs a decision about relocating or regenerating the file, which is the repository owner's; (b) the ASIL field on FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 still carries no justification and the validator still raises an open finding for it - that is a separate condition, not part of this finding, and inventing a justification for it would be fabrication; (c) FB2-SAF-SGO-000001's ASIL remains a hypothetical value in a fictional project and is not a determination for the real product, which has never undergone a HARA. CORRECTION TO REVISION 1: revision 1 required that the document 'state that no functional safety concept or technical safety concept record exists to support a determination, citing CORR-COV-010'. That requirement is obsolete as written. FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 exist as of 2026-09-29. The document now states the accurate position instead: the concepts exist, they are synthetic, each disclaims any ASIL capability in its own limitations field, the asil field on the safety goal is still unjustified and still flagged by the validator, and no HARA has been performed on the real product.

remediation_performed.authorization: The repository owner gave explicit instruction to amend this file, after being told it lay outside the docs/artifacts write boundary and had been logged as a finding rather than edited. That instruction is the sole authority for the out-of-boundary write. It is recorded here so the change is traceable rather than silent, which is the failure mode this finding was raised to prevent. No other file outside docs/artifacts/ was modified, and no foxBMS source, test, config or build file was touched.
edits: Inserted a 'READ FIRST' block immediately below the H1 stating that the document is a synthetic corpus and not a conformity or certification package; that it asserts no ISO 26262 or IEC 61508 compliance; that no ASPICE capability level is claimed; that every ASIL label is hypothetical and not assigned to the real product; that no artifact is human-approved, tool-qualified or production-authorized; and that authoring was automated review, which is not independence and not human confirmation.

Line 19: deleted 'Provides evidence for compliance with ISO 26262, IEC 61508, and other applicable safety standards'. Replaced with an explicit statement that traceability demonstrates that a coherent record chain exists and is navigable, and that it does not demonstrate correctness or satisfy any standard's obligations.

Line 23: replaced 'Safety Requirements (ASIL-D, ASIL-B)' with a statement carrying hypothetical ASIL-D and ASIL-B labels for a fictional reference project, explicitly not assigned to the real foxBMS 2 product, which has never undergone a HARA.
Document control block: version 1.0 -> 2.0, date 2026-09-11 -> 2026-09-29, project title qualified as a synthetic reference corpus, classification qualified as not a certification package.

Section 9 retitled from 'Standards Compliance Traceability' to 'Standards Reference Traceability', with a preamble stating it is a reference index and not a compliance matrix, and that the clause identifiers are the corpus's own references rather than verified citations against the normative standards.

The three ASIL occurrences in the data tables (lines 88, 89, 98) relabelled to 'hypothetical ASIL-D' and 'hypothetical ASIL-B' so the qualification is visible at the point of use, not only in the header.
Section 10.1 coverage table marked STALE with a pointer to the tool-computed figures, because its counts predate the corpus expansion and understate it.

The validator and the renderer still do not read it.

Replaced it with a document-control table stating: authored by an automated agent session with the corpus role names explicitly labelled as fictional labels; reviewed by nobody; approved by nobody; no independent confirmation; human approval status pending for this document and pending for all 220 indexed records; production_authorized false for this document and for all 220; tool qualification none; certification none; ASPICE capability level not asserted.

Manual edits will be overwritten on next generation.' with a provenance section stating that the file is hand-authored, that no tool reads or regenerates it, that git ls-tree at the pinned commit contains no TRACEABILITY entry so it is not a build output, that it is therefore subject to undetectable drift, which surfaces are authoritative, and that the durable fix has not been implemented.

remediation_performed.verified_by_revision_3: A script was written to check the corrected file mechanically. It resolves every identifier-shaped string in the document against the corpus index, the assumption, parameter, link and source registries, the variant matrix and the short scenario-id key space, and separately asserts that no APPROVED status, no approver field, no named reviewer, no conformity or certification claim, no capability-level claim, no IEC 61508 clause row, no 'automatically generated' claim, and no percentage without a stated method survives. All three checks pass. The six identifiers that do not resolve are all named on lines that say what they are: four of them are cited only to record that the previous revision of the file was wrong, and two are the declared forward reference recorded as finding FB2-REV-FND-000030. corpus.py validate, corpus.py check and corpus.py selftest were re-run after the edit and are unchanged.

residual_risk: The file remains outside the corpus toolchain's reach. The validator does not read it, the renderer does not regenerate it, and the guard-field discipline that governs every generated surface has no authority over it. It can therefore drift back toward the original overclaim, and nothing in the current tooling will detect that. The header added in the revision-2 remediation, and the provenance and document-control sections added in revision 3, are human-maintained controls, not machine-enforced ones. The revision-2 pass is the proof: it fixed the three defects it looked for and left a fabricated approval sign-off, a false provenance claim and two IEC 61508 rows in place, and no gate fired. The durable fix is to either relocate the file under docs/artifacts/ and generate it from the canonical records, or to place it under the same document-control regime as the rest of the tree. Neither has been done, and both are the repository owner's decision. Until then, a reviewer must read its header to know what it is, which is precisely the dependency this finding identified.
closure_note: Two premises of revision 1 are now outdated and are corrected here rather than left to mislead. First, revision 1 recorded, correctly at the time, that no functional safety concept and no technical safety concept record existed, and that this absence was why no ASIL determination was supported. As of 2026-09-29 the corpus does contain FB2-SAF-FSC-000001 (functional safety concept) and FB2-SAF-TSC-000001 (technical safety concept), authored under the same session. That closes the record-level gap the finding described. It does NOT change the remediation and does NOT make the ASIL value a determination of the real product: both concepts are synthetic records in a hypothetical project and each states in its own limitations field that it establishes no ASIL capability for any real product, the asil field on FB2-SAF-SGO-000001 still carries no justification, the corpus's own validator still raises an open finding for it on every run, and no HARA has been performed on the real foxBMS 2 product. The ASIL qualification in the document header therefore remains correct and is still required. Second, revision 1 and revision 2 both required that the document be brought inside the controlled area. That has NOT been done: the file is still at the repository root and is still hand-authored. The repository owner authorised amending it, not relocating it.

disposition_note: This record uses disposition 'accepted', which is a member of the enum in docs/artifacts/schemas/finding.schema.json (accepted | rejected | deferred | partial | in_progress). It is necessary to state plainly that THE CORPUS VOCABULARY FOR 'accepted' IS AMBIGUOUS, because the meaning it is given here is not defined anywhere and inventing a definition would repeat the defect this record exists to correct. What is actually observable: (1) the finding schema's disposition property carries only the description 'Disposition of the finding' and defines no semantics; (2) of the 30 records in reviews/findings/, 23 carry disposition 'accepted' and 7 carry 'partial', and 16 of those 23 'accepted' records have a resolution that opens with the words 'NOT RESOLVED' - so corpus practice contradicts any claim that 'accepted' means closed; (3) docs/artifacts/schemas/execution.schema.json uses the same word in a DIFFERENT enum, an anomaly disposition of (accepted | deferred | fixed | wontfix | investigating), where 'accepted' sits beside 'fixed' and 'wontfix' and plainly denotes a known limitation rather than a closed defect. No written schema-level source defines 'accepted' as 'closed' for a finding. THEREFORE, and without asserting any corpus convention: in THIS record, 'accepted' means the specific thing stated in the resolution - the remediation described in remediation_performed was performed, the file was read back and re-verified, and the condition this finding described no longer holds in the file. The residual risk that the file can drift back, because it is outside the toolchain's reach, is recorded in residual_risk and is NOT closed by this disposition. A reader who needs the resolution status of any other finding must read that finding's own resolution field, not this note and not the disposition value.
